name: Isla de San Simón (concentration camp), Ría de Vigo
story: Galicia fell to the coup within days in July 1936, and the rearguard repression was severe. The small island of San Simón, a former lazaretto in the Ría de Vigo, became a concentration camp and penal colony for political prisoners — first from Vigo and Pontevedra, later from across Spain, including many older prisoners. Overcrowding, hunger and disease killed hundreds (around 250 in 1941 alone), and some inmates were taken out and shot. Declared a Bien de Interés Cultural in 1999, the island is now a cultural centre dedicated partly to memory.
see: The restored island buildings, bridge to San Antón islet, and memorial and literary route; guided tours explain the camp period.
plan: Visits by written request to the Xunta de Galicia; groups must arrange their own boat. About 2 hours.
